title: Word formation for Use of English Part 3
tagline: One root, four jobs: noun, verb, adjective, adverb — plus the prefix that flips it.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 3 — word formation
Writing Parts 1 and 2 — precise, varied vocabulary
why: Part 3 gives you a root word and expects you to reshape it: add a suffix to make a noun or adjective, or a prefix to make it negative. Reading quickly, it's easy to miss whether the gap actually needs a plural, a negative, or a completely different word class — which is exactly what this part of the exam is testing.

diagrams.title: Reading the sentence: plural or negative?

rows.label: What changes
cells: add a prefix (un-/in-/im-/il-/ir-/dis-/mis-) to an adjective or verb

rows.label: Example
cells: The teacher marked all fifteen ___ (ESSAY) → essays

rows.label: Trap
cells: easy to forget the -s while you're focused on the root's spelling
easy to reach for -s when the answer actually needs a prefix

head: Category
Typical endings
Example
rows: un-, in-, im-, il-, ir-, dis-, mis-
unfair, indecisive, impolite, illogical, irresponsible, dishonest, misunderstand
a well-known author, a three-hour flight, an English-speaking guide
final -e often drops before a vowel suffix; -y usually becomes -i

use.point: One root, four forms: noun, verb, adjective, adverb

examples.text: Mateo's sudden decision to change subjects surprised everyone.
Was Sofia being decisive, or just impatient?
Liam always speaks so decisively in debates.
It felt completely unfair that the match was postponed twice.
Their instructions were so illogical that nobody followed them properly.
Leaving your phone on the bus was pretty irresponsible, Liam.
Miss Vega is a well-known figure at every regional debate competition.
It was a three-hour bus journey to the trailhead near Ausangate.
examples.note: number stays singular in the compound

use.point: Plural or negative? Reading the sentence before you write anything

examples.text: The form asked for the names of all participants, not just the captain.
examples.note: plural noun, not a negative form

examples.text: Sofia's answer in the interview was completely unexpected.

watch_out.wrong: The pilot's sudden indecisive cost them the match.
watch_out.right: The pilot's sudden indecision cost them the match.
watch_out.why: After 'sudden', the sentence needs a noun, not an adjective.

watch_out.wrong: It would be very unfairly to blame just one player.
watch_out.right: It would be very unfair to blame just one player.
watch_out.why: After 'be', the sentence needs an adjective, not an adverb.
The negative prefix before a word starting with l is il-, not in-.

watch_out.wrong: The mistake was totally unresponsible of him.
watch_out.right: The mistake was totally irresponsible of him.
watch_out.why: The negative prefix before a word starting with r is ir-, not un-.

watch_out.wrong: The teacher marked all fifteen essay.
watch_out.why: 'Fifteen' signals that a plural is needed here, not a negative form.
In a compound adjective before a noun, the number stays singular: three-hour, not three-hours.

dialogue.title: Essay feedback
dialogue.context: Miss Vega is handing back essays, and Mateo, Sofia, Liam and Nadia compare notes on the comments they got.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Overall, good work. Liam, your conclusion needed more confidence — you kept hedging.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: I know, I felt pretty indecisive about the ending.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Mine got marked down for being repetitive, apparently.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Mine too — but Miss Vega said the creativity in my introduction saved it.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: It did. Mateo, yours was strong, but a couple of sentences felt illogical — the order didn't quite make sense.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Fair enough. I wrote it the night before, so that was pretty irresponsible of me.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: At least none of us got 'unclear', like last term.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: True. That was genuinely unfair — half the class got that comment.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: For the next essay, focus on compound adjectives — things like well-written or fast-paced. They make your style sound more natural.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: So instead of 'a play that lasts two hours', we'd write 'a two-hour play'?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Noted. Let's aim for fewer corrections next time.

items.sentence: Sofia felt a strange sense of ___ after the interview.
items.why: 'a sense of' is followed by a noun

items.sentence: The volcano trek turned out to be far more ___ than we expected.
Their explanation was completely ___ — nobody could follow it.
items.why: an adjective is needed after 'was', and the negative prefix il- fits before a word starting with l

items.sentence: Liam's ___ during the debate surprised everyone — he's usually so quiet.
items.why: the subject of the sentence needs a noun

items.sentence: It would be ___ to leave without saying thank you to the host family.
items.why: an adjective is needed after 'would be', and the negative prefix im- fits before p

items.sentence: Nadia reacted ___ when she heard the news.
items.why: an adverb is needed to modify the verb 'reacted'

items.sentence: The teacher's feedback on the essay was really ___.
items.why: an adjective is needed after 'was really'

practice.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form of the word in brackets.

items.sentence: Mateo's ___ (DECIDE) to switch subjects surprised his parents.
The trek to Rainbow Mountain was physically ___ (DEMAND).
Sofia's essay showed real ___ (MATURE) for someone her age.
It seems ___ (RESPONSIBLE) to leave the stove on when nobody's home.
The coach praised the team's ___ (ACHIEVE) at the tournament.
Liam's argument was ___ (CONVINCE) enough to change Miss Vega's mind.
The results were completely ___ (SURPRISE) to everyone in the class.

practice.instructions: Use the word given in capitals to form a word that fits in the gap.

items.first: The pilot's sudden ___ cost the team the match.
Miss Vega was impressed by the ___ of the students' presentation.
items.second_start: Miss Vega was impressed by the

items.first: Nadia's parents were proud of her ___ on the school council.
items.second_start: Nadia's parents were proud of her

items.first: The new rule seemed completely ___ to most students.
The hikers were warned about the ___ weather conditions in the mountains.
items.second_start: The hikers were warned about the

summary: One root usually has a noun, verb, adjective and adverb form: decide, decision, decisive, decisively.
The negative prefix depends on the first letter of the root: un-/in- are common, but il- (before l), im- (before p or m) and ir- (before r) are fixed.
Compound adjectives (well-known, three-hour, English-speaking) stay singular before a noun even when the idea is plural.
Before you add a suffix, check whether the gap actually needs a plural (-s) instead of a different word form.
Always read the whole sentence first — the word class you need depends on what comes right before and after the gap.
